rationale:
The Governance Board finds that the POST-700 governance framework has achieved HARDENED status at both the design and partial-enforcement layers. The S725 Board's 8 conditions have been resolved (2), partially resolved (3), or escalated with documented paths (3). The evidence is unanimous across 18+ agent outputs: the framework prevents recurrence of all 6 documented historical defect patterns, the learner pool is structurally secure (2,181 Certified, 0 actual DL-008), 0 BLOCKING governance risks remain (down from 5 at S723), and the governance guard has been upgraded from DL-029-vulnerable FM-001 to string-aware object extraction (27/27 tests PASS).

The Board's distinction between HARDENED and FULLY OPERATIONAL — established in S725 — remains operative. The framework is HARDENED: all standards are published, all specifications are complete, all 6 historical incidents would have been prevented (validated by Agent N), the enforcement architecture is specified (21 mechanisms: 12 mechanical + 9 procedural), and the design-activation gap is reduced from 24 points (S725: 23/25 design vs. 17/25 activation) to a narrower 6 points (S726: governance guard upgraded, baselines remediated, closure gate designed, acceptance registry created). The four remaining activation gaps (AM-1 upgrade, ownership acceptances, G-NEW integration, Rule 6 implementation) are execution items — not design defects.

The single most critical finding that prevents FULLY OPERATIONAL certification is the 0/6 ownership acceptance state. Per Stewardship Principle 2, unilateral assignment without acceptance is invalid. All 6 deadlines passed at S726 T0 without a single acceptance. The Board does not treat this as a design failure — the acceptance registry, evidence standards, and escalation chain are all properly specified. This is an activation sequencing failure: the design sessions (S725) defined ownership but operational roles were not spawned to accept. The framework correctly identifies this state and escalates it to the Governance Board. The Board's role at this juncture is to enforce the escalation — not to downgrade the HARDENED verdict.

The governance guard upgrade is substantive and effective. Agent K's simulation conclusively demonstrates that the new approach (extractObjectsFromText + within-object property access) achieves 100% DL-008 detection (vs. 0% for the old window-scan) with zero false positives (vs. 100% false-positive rate for the old approach). The DL-029 vulnerability — cross-object CC contamination — is eliminated. The remaining gap (AM-1 full-file parse vs. AM-2 object extraction) is enhancement, not regression: the current implementation correctly handles all pack formats including Pack B CC-before-QID ordering.

However, the Board notes with concern three documentation integrity gaps: (1) no REVISION_HISTORY.md entry for the governance guard code change (AGENTS.md §12 violation), (2) no governance-guard.js backup on disk despite the audit report claiming one was created (BACKUP_PROTOCOL.md partial violation), and (3) the SESSION_STATUS_2026-07-24.md handoff document remains wholly stale (8 phantom references, 2,031 vs. 2,181 certified, 67 phantom DL-008). AGENTS.md §9 directs all sessions to read this file first — meaning every new session starts with incorrect data. The Board requires this document to be superseded before S727.

precedent: This decision mirrors the S725 Board's distinction between HARDENED (design complete, standards published, rules binding) and FULLY OPERATIONAL (every enforcement mechanism implemented and activated). The S725 Board declared POST-700 GOVERNANCE HARDENED with 8 conditions. S726 has resolved 2 conditions (COND-02 baselines cleanup, governance guard intermediate upgrade), partially resolved 3 (COND-01 AM-1 spec complete but not implemented, COND-04 acceptance registry created but 0 acceptances, COND-05 baselines partially remediated), and carried forward 3 to S727+. The 0/6 ownership acceptance state is the single most critical gap — but it is a procedural activation gap, not a design defect. The framework correctly identifies this state, properly escalates it to the Governance Board, and has documented succession paths if owners remain unresponsive. This is the framework working as designed.
dissenting_notes: A minority position within the Board considered ADDITIONAL ENFORCEMENT REQUIRED on the grounds that 0/6 ownership acceptances constitutes a genuine governance failure under the framework's own Principle 2, and that HARDENED implies the framework can actually prevent recurrence — not just document how it would. The majority position (adopted) holds that HARDENED is a design-level certification and that the 0/6 acceptance gap is an activation sequencing failure. The distinction is documented and preserved. The Board will revisit at S727 T0: if ownership acceptances remain at 0/6 past the escalated deadline, the determination will shift to ADDITIONAL ENFORCEMENT REQUIRED — because the framework's own enforcement mechanism (Governance Board escalation) will have been tested and found insufficient if the governance actor itself fails to execute against a documented escalation.
